scope: M0 task-model fit smoke tests; not the M6 12-task evaluation

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

tasks.input: Based only on the provided ReAct pages, explain how reasoning and acting interact. Give two concise claims with source page and short verbatim supporting quotes. State one limitation of the available evidence. Do not claim production reliability.
rubric: Two claims explain the relationship between reasoning, actions and observations
Every source ID exists and quoted text is found on the declared page
Answer does not claim checkpointing, exactly-once or production reliability

tasks.input: Review the supplied Reflexion excerpt: summarize the mechanism, explain the role of feedback and memory, and distinguish this from updating model weights. Use at most three supported claims. Mark details outside this excerpt as unknown; do not invent benchmark comparisons.
rubric: Describes language-based reflection/feedback and episodic memory
Does not describe it as weight fine-tuning
Citations match pages and support each mechanism claim
Separates excerpt-supported findings from missing full-paper details

tasks.input: Compare ReAct and Reflexion on interaction with the environment and use of feedback/memory, based only on these excerpts. Give at least one supported claim for each paper and a short practical design implication clearly marked as an inference. Do not rank effectiveness across incomparable experiments.
rubric: Includes both papers with source-bound claims
Distinguishes within-task reasoning/action from reflection over feedback
Design implication is explicitly labeled inference
Does not assert an unsupported cross-paper performance winner
